text:
maria: Heads up — my local sample-app (leaky-bucket client throttle + pagination prefetch) started spitting a bunch of 401s during a synthetic burst test just now.
kevin: 401s vs 429s? share logs plz
maria: Minimal log excerpt:
2026-03-22T14:10:12.123Z WARN http: request failed status=429 route="/v1/generate"
2026-03-22T14:10:12.456Z INFO auth: starting token refresh
2026-03-22T14:10:12.460Z DEBUG http: retrying request id=abc123 attempt=1
2026-03-22T14:10:12.462Z ERROR http: request failed status=401 route="/v1/generate" id=abc123

maria: TL;DR the SDK retries after a 429, but the retry runs before the token refresh completes so it replays the original Authorization header -> 401.
jen: oof. JS SDK uses a shared token promise but our retry path doesn't await it consistently. If refresh starts and retries fire, you can end up replaying stale creds.
samir: saw same pattern in Go sample-app — heavy pagination prefetch plus aggressive local bursts amplifies the problem. multiple goroutines all try to refresh concurrently.
kevin: So two interacting problems: client-side burst behavior (too permissive defaults + prefetch) and retry logic that doesn't block on in-flight refresh.
maria: Proposed fixes: make retry path await token refresh (or use a lock), token store returns existing refresh promise, add jittered backoff, lower sample-app leaky-bucket defaults, disable pagination prefetch by default.
jen: For defaults I suggest rate=20 ops/sec, burst=40 for single-process sample apps. Current sample-app default was 100/s which is too high.
samir: And make pagination prefetch opt-in (current default prefetch=4 pages was chewing tokens during downstream slowness).
kevin: Example pseudo-change (JS): await tokenStore.getValidToken(); try { await sendRequest(); } catch (e) { if (e.status === 429) { await tokenStore.getValidToken(); await sleep(withJitter(calcBackoff(attempt))); retry(); } }
jen: +1. Also add guard in tokenStore.refresh() that returns the existing promise while refresh is ongoing.
maria: I'll open a PR to change retry path, lower defaults to rate=20/burst=40, set pagination.prefetch=0 by default, and add deterministic tests that simulate token expiry during retry.
kevin: Please add a test that stubs tokenStore.refresh() to pause so we reliably reproduce the race.
samir: I'll mirror equivalent changes in Go sample-app and add integration test there too.
jen: Docs: I'll update onboarding quickstart and sample-app README to call out recommended throttle settings and the token-rotation/retry behavior. Add an example YAML config block: client_throttle: rate: 20 # ops/sec burst: 40 retry: base_ms: 200 max_ms: 2000 jitter: true pagination: prefetch: 0
maria: Quick actions: maria -> PR for JS sample-app + tests; jen -> docs update; samir -> Go sample-app changes; kevin -> review PRs + run sanity on Dedicated
kevin: I'll add a DevEx console dashboard card for "client-side 401 spike" to catch regressions.
ci-bot: CI started for branch maria/fix-retry-token-race :github:
maria: Short-term mitigation: set sample-app env THROTTLE_RATE=10 and disable pagination prefetch while fixes roll.
samir: noted, I'll flip the Go env too.
kevin: Good detective work everyone. :thumbsup:
maria: I'll post the PR link when ready and update this thread. End of thread.
